title: AlexNet: the image-recognition breakthrough
idea: A deep network, trained on more than a million labelled photos using graphics cards built for video games, won the 2012 ImageNet image-recognition contest by a wide margin. After it, deep learning became the default approach to computer vision.

cameFrom.note: The whole network, eight learning layers deep, was trained end to end by passing the error backwards.
The deep learning revival had shown that deep networks were worth the effort, and AlexNet came out of the same Toronto group.

cameFrom.label: Convolutional networks (LeCun and colleagues, 1989)
cameFrom.note: Networks that slide the same small feature detectors across an image, first used to read handwritten zip codes.

cameFrom.label: GPUs
cameFrom.note: Graphics cards do thousands of multiplications at once. Two NVIDIA GTX 580 cards trained the network in five to six days.

cameFrom.label: ImageNet (Fei-Fei Li and colleagues, 2009)
cameFrom.note: A huge labelled photo collection. The 2012 contest used about 1.2 million training images in 1,000 categories.

people.note: Doctoral student of Hinton at the University of Toronto, who wrote the fast graphics-card code that made the training possible.
Doctoral student of Hinton at Toronto, who in 2015 co-founded OpenAI.
Their supervisor at the University of Toronto. The three founded a start-up on this work that Google acquired in 2013.

papers.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 25 (NeurIPS 2012), 1097–1105
papers.summary: It described a network with 60 million parameters, five convolutional layers and three fully connected ones, trained on two graphics cards. It won the 2012 contest with a top-5 error of 15.3 percent, against 26.2 percent for the next best entry. Simple neurons, a trick called dropout and heavy data augmentation made the training work.

steps.heading: Convolution
steps.body: Early layers slide small learned filters across the image. The same filter is reused everywhere, so a detector for an edge or a texture works wherever the edge appears.

steps.heading: Layers of features
steps.body: Later layers combine those features into larger ones, from edges to textures to parts of objects, and the last layers vote on the 1,000 categories.

steps.heading: Simple neurons
steps.body: Each neuron outputs its input if positive and zero otherwise (ReLU). This trains several times faster than the smooth squashing curves used before.

steps.heading: Dropout
steps.body: During training, half the neurons in the large layers are switched off at random for each example. The network cannot lean on any one neuron, so it generalises better.

steps.heading: More data from the same data
steps.body: Random crops and flips of each photo, and small colour changes, multiplied the effective training set and reduced overfitting.

steps.heading: Top-5 error
steps.body: The contest counted an answer as right if the true label was among the network's five best guesses. AlexNet got 15.3 percent wrong; the next best team, using other methods, got 26.2 percent wrong.
